Elena — thanks, quick answers below.

1) Routing: prefer sequential routing in DocuSign to ensure signatory authority is validated in order (Procurement -> Legal -> Exec). We can make procurement a "must sign" first recipient. If Acme requires simultaneous signing for logistics, let me know and we can switch to parallel, but our internal countersign workflow expects to see Procurement signed first.

2) Witness signature: Redwood does not generally require an external witness on DPAs; countersign (internal RDW exec) will be an internal signature only. If Acme's corporate policy mandates a witness, we can add an optional witness recipient. Note that adding witness role will add a manual step (not auto-countersign).

3) Attachments: yes — we will attach the subprocessor matrix and the final redlines as supporting docs inside the envelope. We'll tag the subprocessor matrix as a non-signing document for auditor download.

4) Fallback: Our standard is: DocuSign sequential -> if envelope fails (signer unavailable or eSign rejected) we route to manual countersign path via AdobeSign and escrow PDFs to both parties. That fallback is invoked by legal ops only.

Next steps: I'll prepare the envelope with the following recipients (placeholders) —

  - 2) Acme Legal (sign/ack) — Elena Park
  - 3) Redwood Procurement (review) — David Kim
  - 4) Redwood Legal (sign) — Marissa Cole
  - 5) Redwood Exec (countersign) — Rishi Malhotra (will countersign after preceding signatures)

I'll send an envelope notice with envelope ID and expected SLA (72 hours) once it's set. Attaching our exec authority matrix for clarity.

Thanks,
